subject.title: feat: 0.5.0 API surface — archive policy, publication mechanics, sync locks, secret create-only, Root.walk, cleanup receipts

question: Should the 0.5.0 release include the optional native binding migration and nine-package publishing redesign together with the new TypeScript APIs, or should that release-engineering/security-boundary work be split or deferred?
rationale: The implementation introduces a new package topology and compatibility bridge on a core filesystem-security boundary; code review alone cannot choose the intended public release scope.

options.title: Approve the integrated 0.5.0 scope
options.body: Accept the combined API, native-binding, and release redesign after runtime and upgrade proof demonstrates the intended compatibility and fallback behavior.

options.title: Split the native release work
options.body: Keep the focused TypeScript API additions in this release and move the native package graph plus publishing redesign into a separately reviewed change.

options.title: Defer the native migration
options.body: Retain the existing helper path for 0.5.0 and revisit native bindings once the multi-package publishing contract has a separately approved release plan.

recommendation.title: Approve the integrated 0.5.0 scope
recommendation.body: Accept the combined API, native-binding, and release redesign after runtime and upgrade proof demonstrates the intended compatibility and fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: ctbritt is the strongest available current-main history contact for the adjacent root-boundary behavior, though ownership of the release decision is only weakly established from the available history.
